author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory, reached at GET /specialties.html, lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name on one unpaginated page. Each specialty shows the veterinarians holding it by full name, first then last. Veterinarians holding no specialty appear nowhere on it.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when GET /specialties.html is requested, then every specialty is listed by its stored name on one page, with no pagination
given a specialty that veterinarians hold, when the specialty directory is opened, then each of them is listed under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary" under radiology)
given a veterinarian holding two specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian is listed under each of them (seeded: Linda Douglas under surgery and dentistry)
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it (seeded: James Carter, Sharon Jenkins)
given a specialty held by no veterinarian, when the specialty directory is opened, then it is still listed and shown as held by none rather than left blank (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3)
given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then each specialty appears under its stored name, neither recapitalized nor translated (edge case 4)
given the specialty directory, when it is opened repeatedly, then specialties and the veterinarians under each appear in the same stable order every time (edge case 5)
given the specialty directory, when it is rendered, then it carries the standard navigation of every page (REQ-SYS-001) and any wording it adds is present in every supported language (REQ-LANG-002)
non_goals: Any navigation entry or link from another page to the specialty directory. Owner decision (intake line 1): "The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request." Recorded as an Open Question, not a Non-Goals row, because it is deferred, not declined
Managing veterinarians or specialties (NG-2, unchanged per the owner's decision at intake line 1)
Searching or filtering by specialty; the page lists, it takes no query (NG-9 stands)
A machine-readable form of the specialty directory (compare withdrawn REQ-VET-002)
Translating or recapitalizing stored specialty names
notes: Boundary check: NG-2 is unchanged per the quoted owner decision. NG-9 declines search; this page takes no query, so it does not conflict. REQ-SYS-001 navigation still applies to the new page. Any new page wording falls under REQ-LANG-002 and I18nPropertiesSyncTest; the existing 'none' key may cover the held-by-none text. Reversible decisions taken under the owner's narrowest-reading instruction: (1) a specialty held by no veterinarian is listed and shown as held by none, following the REQ-VET-001 precedent; (2) ordering is only required to be stable, and the exact order is left to design and recorded as an Open Question. PRD delta: banner, Context, Veterinarian directory narrative, Done-when, edge cases 3-5, two Open Questions. No Non-Goals row changed, so there are no scope_overrides. No autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package using only In-force catalog patterns (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog); no new module, no cross-package reference, no new dependency. Three adjustments: (1) a read-only SpecialtyRepository in vet/, following the PetTypeRepository lookup-repository precedent, because 'every specialty the clinic knows' includes specialties no Vet holds and only the specialties table can supply them; it extends Spring Data's bare Repository (like VetRepository), not JpaRepository, so no write method is exposed (NG-2, least privilege). (2) SpecialtyDirectory, an immutable value object in vet/ built by a pure static factory from the specialty list and the vet roster; the grouping and ordering rules live there, below the controller, so they are unit-testable without the framework (Design Principle 4; testing-principles § Test Pyramid). (3) A GET /specialties.html handler on VetController that reads SpecialtyRepository and the cached VetRepository.findAll(), builds the directory, and renders templates/vets/specialtyList.html inside the standard layout fragment. Ordering (the PRD leaves it to design): specialties by name, holders by last name then first name, ties by stored identifier; recorded on the SpecialtyDirectory Contracts row. The PRD's ordering Open Question stays with the owner. Design-doc writes: REQ-VET-003 joined to the Vet, Specialty, VetRepository, VetController, CacheConfiguration Contracts rows; new SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory rows; one invariant sentence; vet/ package line; and the § Scale and Load section (absent until now; doctor template form) with three rows for this slice's path.
integration_points: Binding, GET /specialties.html: binds nothing. No @RequestParam, no @PathVariable, no form object, so there is no request-scoped binding target and no persisted type is bound. The only model attribute is the request-scoped SpecialtyDirectory. A query parameter must not be introduced (NG-9, prd non_goals).

Double, repository boundary in SpecialtyDirectoryTests (unit): none. The factory takes real Specialty and Vet objects constructed in memory, following the existing VetControllerTests helen()/james() construction (testing-principles § Mocking Policy: real objects first). The multi-holding, omission, held-by-none and stable-order rules are tested here.

Double, framework transport in VetControllerTests: MockMvc via the existing @WebMvcTest(VetController.class), the sanctioned mock. Asserts rendering: view name, stored specialty name, holder as 'First Last', the #{none} text under an unheld specialty, an absent vet not rendered, layout navigation present.

Double, SpecialtyRepository in VetControllerTests: a hand-written double, a small in-test implementation of the one-method interface registered through a nested @TestConfiguration, returning fixed Specialty objects. No @MockitoBean for SpecialtyRepository.

Double, VetRepository in VetControllerTests: the existing class-level @MockitoBean and its setup() stubbing of findAll() (James Carter, Helen Leary) is reused unchanged, as tolerated pre-existing usage. Adding no new given(...) stubbing is the target; any new stubbing it needs is a consultation first.

Double, repository boundary for the seeded-data criteria (Linda Douglas under surgery and dentistry; James Carter and Sharon Jenkins absent): real implementation, one GET /specialties.html check in PetClinicIntegrationTests against the seeded H2 database.

Template: specialtyList.html uses th:replace with the layout fragment like vetList.html; the menu argument names no existing nav entry (no nav entry is in scope; prd non_goals). Holder names render with th:text (escaped), never th:utext (security-principles § Realization, XSS row).
Messages: reuse the existing keys specialties, vets, name, none. Any new key lands in every messages*.properties bundle (REQ-LANG-002; I18nPropertiesSyncTest).

patterns.description: Lookup-value repository returning all rows in name order; SpecialtyRepository mirrors it, but on the bare Repository base for read-only surface
Read-only Repository base with @Transactional(readOnly = true); cached findAll() is the roster source
Layout fragment use, 'first last' name rendering, #{none} for an empty holding

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines no equals/hashCode, so Specialty equality is object identity. Vet instances come from the vet cache while the specialty list is loaded fresh, so grouping by Specialty object or Set.contains silently yields empty holder lists.
risks.mitigation: Group by stored identifier (Specialty.getId()), as the SpecialtyDirectory invariant in system-design § Contracts states; a unit test builds the specialty list and the vets' specialties as distinct instances carrying the same id.

risks.risk: Specialty names carry no uniqueness constraint (db/*/schema.sql), and vet names may repeat, so name-only sorting is not a total order and violates PRD edge case 5.
risks.mitigation: Ties are broken by stored identifier, per the SpecialtyDirectory Contracts row.

risks.risk: Specialties path, whole-list read per request (system-design § Scale and Load, 'Specialties' row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one name-ordered repository query, uncached.

risks.risk: Roster path, whole cached read (system-design § Scale and Load, 'Veterinarian roster, whole' row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: reuse the cached VetRepository.findAll(); no new query or cache.

risks.risk: Directory grouping path (system-design § Scale and Load, 'Specialty directory request' row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: one pass grouping holders by specialty identifier, then a Comparator sort; no hand-written structure.

risks.risk: SpecialtyDirectory holding mutable Vet/Specialty entities breaks the closed immutability property; the entity exception does not cover non-entity types (architecture-principles § Scoped exception).
risks.mitigation: The value object copies out the specialty name and holder first/last names into immutable records with List.copyOf; no entity reference escapes into it.

risks.risk: Grouping or ordering logic placed in VetController is a fresh Web controller violation (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, In force).
risks.mitigation: The controller only reads the two repositories, calls the SpecialtyDirectory factory, and selects the view.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit. The PRD file_targets name VetRepository.java, but it needs no change: the cached findAll() already supplies the roster. SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory are additions. Security: the new route exposes the same veterinarian and specialty names /vets.html already publishes; it is read-only and adds no Threat Model row. A repository failure propagates to the existing error page (errors flow outward). A cached vet referencing a specialty id missing from the fresh specialty list is not rendered; that out-of-band staleness falls under system-design Open Question 5. No ADR: the ordering and repository choices constrain no later slice beyond their Contracts rows.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No request input reaches the new route: VetController.showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model) binds no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody, so it adds no injection, mass-assignment or path-resolution surface. A grep -E 'Runtime|ProcessBuilder|JsonTypeInfo|Files\.|@ModelAttribute|@RequestBody|createQuery|nativeQuery' over src/main/java/.../vet/ matched nothing

The data-access query is static and parameterless: SpecialtyRepository.java carries @Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name") with no concatenation. The repository extends the bare Repository and is @Transactional(readOnly = true), so it exposes no write method (least privilege)

XSS control holds: every DB-derived value in templates/vets/specialtyList.html is rendered with escaping th:text (${entry.specialty}, ${holder.firstName + ' ' + holder.lastName}). A grep -E 'utext|__\$\{' on that template matched nothing, which matches the escaping pattern of the neighbouring vet list

Surface widening is stated. The new GET /specialties.html is read-only, unauthenticated like every route in the recorded baseline (system-design.md Security Context), and exposes only specialty names and vet first/last names, which the existing /vets and /vets.html routes already serve. It changes no management or actuator exposure

SpecialtyDirectory copies names into immutable records (List.copyOf), so no mutable JPA entity reaches the view. The controller holds only final repository fields, with no shared mutable state in the singleton

The unpaginated whole-table read is sized in the new system-design.md Scale and Load rows as bounded, out-of-band-only data (NG-2). No request can grow it, so it adds no request-driven unbounded allocation

Null names are not attacker-reachable. db/h2/schema.sql declares specialties.name VARCHAR(80) and vets first_name/last_name VARCHAR(30) as nullable, so a null would make the comparators throw. But no route writes specialties or vets (NG-2), so there is no attacker path. This is noted for robustness only and is not a security finding
No secrets were added: the diff adds no token, password, secret, key or credential-like literal, and git diff shows no change to build.gradle or pom.xml, so there is no new dependency

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Nine files, all in the vet package plus its template and the two briefs. No sensitive paths are touched. The only change to existing code is VetController gaining a SpecialtyRepository constructor argument and one GET /specialties.html handler, and nothing else constructs VetController. The flagged security surface is a parameterless static JPQL query and a route that binds no input and shows only names that /vets.html already shows.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the description says. Holders are grouped by specialty id in one pass over the cached roster. Specialties come from a fresh name-ordered query, and both sorts end in an id tie-break. The template escapes every value with th:text and renders the existing none key under an unheld specialty. No existing behavior changes: the paged vet list, the JSON route, the cache and the layout nav are untouched. The one residual, documented in the design, is that holders come from the vet cache while specialties are read fresh. A null name in out-of-band data would make the comparators throw, and Vet.getSpecialties already has that exposure.

test_adequacy.note: SpecialtyDirectoryTests compare whole expected directories against real entities, and six tests each fail if their rule is removed: multi-holding, omission, held-by-none, match by id rather than instance, name ordering, and the same-name specialty tie-break. The MockMvc tests check rendering and the none text, which the layout does not otherwise contain. The integration test drives the seeded data end to end, including the absence of James Carter and Sharon Jenkins. The one surviving mutant is the holder id tie-break, which only matters for two vets with identical full names.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved in round 1 with no findings. Their recommendations are polish: renaming Entry.specialty, the ordering being done in both the query and the directory, a glossary entry, and two small test gaps. Citations I checked resolve (messages.properties 21-24, SpecialtyDirectoryTests 136/147/156/160, VetControllerTests 107). The unconfigured OWASP scan and the format task the reviewer could not run are standing gaps that build-pass covers.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake: a read-only GET /specialties.html, one unpaginated page, first-then-last names, vets without specialties omitted, and no nav link (layout.html is unchanged). The order was left open by the owner and was fixed by the design-block. It is recorded as an open question. There were no design revisions and no consultations. It changes no existing behavior, and its tests would catch removal of every rule except the identical-name holder tie-break.
